English: Soldiers Hut
A basic shelter of wood, thatch, and earth for a small number of soldiers. The first step toward a permanent garrison.
Guard Quarters
Simple wooden barracks and a central fire-pit, these quarters allow a small guard unit to rest, drill, and organize patrols.
Timber Barracks
Wooden barracks with a crude mess hall and armory. These provide shelter and discipline for a modest garrison.
Stone Barracks
Solid stone barracks with reinforced doors and walls, providing protection and permanence to the castles defenders.
Expanded Barracks
A substantial expansion with multiple stone wings, proper bunks for men-at-arms, and improved command facilities.
Training Yard
An open yard with targets, dummies, and obstacle courses where troops drill, improving discipline and morale.
Drill Hall
A covered hall for year-round drills and advanced tactics, fostering a core of professional soldiers.
Garrison House
A fortified living complex for elite guards, with ample stores and command posts for rapid deployment.
Warriors Dormitory
Large dormitories with armories and mess halls, supporting a standing force and swift mobilization in times of siege.
Grand Garrison
A vast, multi-level military complex with barracks, armories, drill halls, and officer quarters for a true fortress garrison.
